To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the EU ETS needs to be reformed in order to provide the right incentives for low carbon investment.
the EU ETS is currently not fit for purpose and that it should be complemented by a rising carbon price floor to drive investments in low carbon technology R&D.
a price floor can be an effective tool to re-affirm the role of EU ETS as a central pillar in European efforts to decarbonize the economy.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: How can the EU ETS be designed in order to provide a clear signal to the market and to guide investments in low carbon technology? What are the distributional implications of different policy instruments? How can these instruments be designed in order not to undermine political support?

the following questions: How can a carbon price floor be designed to provide a clear signal for low carbon investment, and to ensure political support and long term effectiveness? What are the distributional impacts of a carbon price floor, how can they be managed, and what are the implications for the EU ETS?

the question whether the EU ETS is an effective instrument for achieving the long term decarbonisation goals set out in the Paris Agreement, in the context of a global carbon market that is currently not in operation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
1. The EU Emission Trading System (ETS) is in a crisis due to persistently low allowance (EUA ) prices.

(1) a price floor is needed to ensure that the EU ETS can effectively support European decarbonization, (2) a price floor should be introduced at the European level, (3) the price floor should rise over time, (4) the price floor needs to be complemented by targeted and temporary compensation models and public investments into technology R&D to ensure its political acceptance and to avoid adverse distributional impacts.

a carbon price floor is required to re affirm the EU ETS in its role as the central pillar for European decarbonization, but that the EU ETS reform process offers an entry point for introducing a carbon price floor, and that a carbon price ceiling is required to avoid the risk that allowance prices rise to levels that are politically unacceptable.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the EU ETS is currently failing to achieve its environmental objectives and to provide an adequate signal for investment in low carbon technologies.
a carbon price floor should be introduced at an economically significant and rising level to ensure the long-term effectiveness of the EU Emissions Trading System.
the EU ETS is currently not fulfilling its purpose.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the EU ETS needs to be strengthened to reaffirm its role as the central pillar for European decarbonization and to avoid a costly decoupling of the EU Emissions Trading System (EU ETS) from the rest of the world.
the EU ETS is not working well in the context of ambitious European decarbonization goals, and that the recent EU ETS Reform proposal is insufficient to tackle this problem.
a carbon price floor should start with a level that is economically significant.
